claims.text: Sample Consistency methods outperform Token Level Probability and Confidence Elicitation methods for quantifying LLM uncertainty in medical clinical reasoning tasks.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding achieves discrimination ROC AUC performance between 0.68 and 0.79.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding exhibits poor calibration due to value clustering between 0.8 and 1.0.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation achieves discrimination ROC AUC performance between 0.66 and 0.74.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation yields lower Expected Calibration Error and Brier scores compared to Sentence Embedding methods.
Uncertainty metrics exhibit higher discriminative performance on diagnostic reasoning tasks than on treatment selection tasks.
Confidence Elicitation methods consistently overestimate LLM model confidence when answering medical questions.

evidence.description: Sample Consistency methods generally outperformed Token Level Probability and Confidence Elicitation methods for both diagnosis and treatment selection tasks.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding achieved the highest discrimination performance (ROC AUC 0.68–0.79).
Sample Consistency methods that used Sentence Embeddings demonstrated poor calibration due to their limited range of values, clustering composite cosine similarity between 0.8 and 1.0.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation achieved the second-best discrimination (ROC AUC 0.66-0.74).
GPT Annotation yielded lower (better) Expected Calibration Error and Brier scores compared to Sentence Embedding methods.
Nearly all uncertainty metrics had better discriminative performance with diagnosis rather than treatment selection questions.
Calibration plots show Confidence Elicitation methods are nearly universally overconfident across evaluated settings and models.

methodologies.name: Two-step Confidence Elicitation
methodologies.description: The LLM generates a response to a medical question, and then the entire question-response pair is resubmitted to the LLM to rate uncertainty on a score from 0 to 100.
datasets: New England Journal of Medicine Case Report Series

methodologies.name: Token Level Probabilities
methodologies.description: Uncertainty metrics are calculated using either the average token probabilities or the minimum token probability across tokens in the LLM answer.
datasets: New England Journal of Medicine Case Report Series

methodologies.name: Sample Consistency
methodologies.description: Inter-response agreement is measured across 15 forward passes per question using either GPT-4 Annotation or Sentence Embedding distance (e5-small-v2 and S-PubMedBERT).
datasets: New England Journal of Medicine Case Report Series

limitations.text: Sample Consistency methods require multiple times more compute because the model must be run many times to calculate inter-response agreement, making them computationally costly and slow.
The evaluation was limited to US-centric question sets and the English language, preventing generalization to non-English languages and non-US clinical contexts.
Findings cannot be generalized to models that are fine-tuned specifically on medical text.
Ensemble uncertainty estimation methods are computationally expensive and impractical for clinical use requiring HIPAA-level security.

future_work.text: Iterate on proposed uncertainty metrics and utilize the open dataset as a benchmark for further evaluation.
